newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ sees yr profit around NZ$50 mln.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ sees yr profit around NZ$50 mln.

text.p: Power New Zealand Ltd said on Friday it expected its 1995/96 year profit to be in the region of NZ$50 million.

Chairman Don Stanley said the profit would be slightly lower than anticipated, due to the higher cost of electricity purchases caused by national grid operator Transpower's recently announced pricing policies.
Earlier the company reported a half year net profit of NZ$27.83 million, against $23.08 million in the corresponding period last year.

Continued economic growth throughout the company's network saw total revenue for the period improve 16.7 percent to NZ$182.5 million, while further efficiency gains meant earnings per share for the half year rose to NZ 18.4 cents from 15.2 cents.
The interim dividend was lifted to 11 cents per share from 9.2 cents.
Stanley said the higher result reflected the benefits of the company having its networks located within some of the fastest growing regions within New Zealand.
"This, allied with our continuing programmes to reduce costs and improve services standards, has meant a further strengthening of our performance," he said.
Stanley said adjustments of the company's domestic prices, effective from December 1, would result in an increase for average domestic customer of around NZ$1.50 a week.
"This change continues the rebalancing process between the company's domestic and commercial tariffs which is essential for it to remain competitive in a deregulated power market.
"It also represents a recovery of the increased wholesale costs which make up some 70 percent of the company's domestic power prices," Stanley said.
